Fix cosmo's evaluation failure that has blocked the nightly flake.lock update for four nights (PR #678 open since 2026-07-28, CI red on 07-28/29/30/31; last lock landed was #677 on 07-27). Normal cosmo PR flow. KEEP COMMENTS EXTREMELY COMPRESSED / high information density — standing maintainer preference.

ROOT CAUSE (already diagnosed — do not re-investigate): nixpkgs PR #450096, merged 2026-07-25, merged the Overseerr and Jellyseerr projects into a single project named 'Seerr' (Jellyseerr's codebase is the base). 'services.overseerr' was REMOVED, with an entry in nixos/modules/rename.nix reading: '`services.overseerr` has been replaced by `services.seerr` as the project has been merged with Jellyseerr under Seerr.' It is a hard removal (mkRemovedOptionModule), so evaluation throws:
    Failed assertions:
    - The option definition `services.overseerr' in `.../modules/media-server/default.nix' no longer has any effect; please remove it.
classic-laddie is the only host importing modules/media-server, so it is the only failing build-nixos job; the 'check' job fails for the same reason because nix flake check evaluates every host.

THE CHANGE — keep it MINIMAL and scoped to unblocking evaluation:
1. modules/media-server/default.nix (~line 116): rename the option block
       services.overseerr = { enable = true; openFirewall = true; };
   to
       services.seerr = { enable = true; openFirewall = true; };
   Both options exist on services.seerr with the same meaning. Verify against the upstream module at nixos/modules/services/misc/seerr.nix in the pinned nixpkgs before committing.

2. DO NOT change the port anywhere. Seerr's default port is still 5055, identical to Overseerr's, so these all remain correct and MUST be left alone:
   - the caddy virtualHosts 'overseerr' and 'overseerr.local' with 'reverse_proxy localhost:5055' (~lines 188-195)
   - the entry 'overseerr' in the hostname list (~line 164)
   - overseerrUrl = "http://localhost:5055" in hosts/classic-laddie/default.nix (~line 158), which is reel-life's config option name, not a nixpkgs option
   Those vhost names are DNS labels matching a record on the LAN router; renaming them would break that record for no benefit. Leave every hostname as-is.

3. Update only those comments that are now factually wrong (e.g. a comment naming Overseerr as the service being configured). Terse. Do not do a cosmetic sweep of the word 'overseerr'.

VERIFY (this is the whole point — these are the two currently-failing jobs):
   nix build .#nixosConfigurations.classic-laddie.config.system.build.toplevel --dry-run
   nix flake check
Both MUST pass. Also dry-run makers-nix and johnny-walker to confirm no regression. Do NOT do a full real build.

PR BODY must state plainly, because it has a live consequence the maintainer needs to see at review time:
- what upstream changed and why evaluation broke;
- that four nightly lock updates (PR #678) are blocked behind this;
- that Seerr's state directory is chosen by stateVersion — 'useNewConfigLocation = lib.versionAtLeast config.system.stateVersion "26.05"' — and classic-laddie is on 25.11, so seerr will use StateDirectory 'jellyseerr' (/var/lib/jellyseerr/config), which does NOT exist on the host;
- that the existing data lives at /var/lib/overseerr (service currently active) and will be ORPHANED, not deleted, so Seerr comes up as a fresh install until a separate data migration is performed;
- that pointing services.seerr.configDir at the old path does not work, because DynamicUser derives the uid from the service name so ownership will not match.
Do NOT attempt the data migration in this PR and do not add any preStart/tmpfiles copy logic — the migration is being handled separately as a deliberate root operation.

Title: 'fix(media-server): services.overseerr -> services.seerr (upstream merge into Seerr)'.
